d: The band of cervix between the original and the active squamocolumnar junction, where columnar epithelium has undergone squamous metaplasia; its immature cells are the target of high-risk HPV.
A benign mucus-filled cyst that forms when metaplastic squamous epithelium covers the opening of an endocervical crypt and traps its secretions; it needs no treatment.
A squamous cell showing HPV cytopathic effect: an enlarged, wrinkled, hyperchromatic (raisinoid) nucleus with a clear perinuclear halo; typical of LSIL and condyloma.
Strong, continuous p16 immunostaining across the lower epithelium; it reflects E7 inactivation of Rb and supports an HPV-driven high-grade lesion (HSIL).
Magnified examination of the cervix after acetic acid, which turns dysplastic epithelium white so abnormal areas can be biopsied; the diagnostic step after an abnormal screening result.
Excision of the transformation zone with a thin electrified wire loop to treat HSIL; it removes less tissue than a cold-knife cone but can still cause cervical insufficiency.
